guides.treatment_action:
Recommended treatment actions:  
- Apply the latest security patches and updates from Microsoft to address CVE-2020-1472, CVE-2020-1350, CVE-2017-0144, and CVE-2021-31166 on all affected hosts.  
- Disable or configure Netlogon and DNS services on SRV-01 and SRV-02 to restrict unnecessary network communication.  
- Implement network segmentation to isolate SRV-01 (Domain Controller) and SRV-02 (DNS Server) from less secure segments.  
- Configure firewall rules to block unauthorized access to SRV-03 (File Server) and SRV-04 (Application Server) ports used by SMB, WinRM, and web applications.  
- Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for WinRM and disable plaintext authentication on SRV-03 and SRV-04.  
- Conduct a vulnerability scan using automated tools (e.g., Nessus, OpenVAS) to identify residual risks after patching.  
- Perform penetration testing on SRV-01, SRV-02, SRV-03, and SRV-04 to validate the effectiveness of applied controls.  
- Update application configurations on SRV-04 to mitigate CVE-2021-44228 (Log4j) by disabling remote code execution features.  
- Implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) on SRV-04 to filter malicious traffic targeting the web application.  
- Enable logging and monitoring for all network services on SRV-01, SRV-02, SRV-03, and SRV-04, with alerts for suspicious activity.  
- Review and update the information security requirements in project management (Control 5.8) to include network service hardening as a mandatory deliverable.  
- Schedule regular audits of network service configurations to ensure alignment with ISO 27002:2022 Control 8.21 and 8.8.
